To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
IF-1, EF-Tu (and EF-Ts), IF-3, and EF-G have a common ancestor, and that the evolutionary history of these factors of protein synthesis can be explained by a duplication/fusion mechanism.
the proteins involved in protein synthesis have arisen from an ancestral gene sequence by gene duplication/fusion.

(i) the protein factors involved in the translation of the genetic code share a common ancestry; (ii) this ancestry can be traced to an ancient RNA binding protein that was involved in the regulation of gene expression; and (iii) the evolution of this ancestral protein into the modern protein synthesis factors was the result of three consecutive duplication/fusion events that would have taken place prior to the divergence of the modern superkingdoms.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the origin and evolution of the protein synthesis factors and how these factors may be related to each other through a common ancestry.
the evolutionary origin of the factors that mediate translation in living organisms.
the evolution of the protein synthesis factors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
IF-3, IF-2 and IF-1, EF-Tu and EF-Ts, EF-G and EF-Ts constitute a protein superfamily of protein synthesis factors that is the result of a duplication/fusion mechanism.
the origin of the protein synthesis factors is a result of a series of gene duplication/fusions events which took place before the divergence among the three superkingdons.
the protein synthesis factors are a family of proteins which have evolved from a common ancestor by a series of gene duplication and fusion events.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the origin of the protein synthesis factors is the product of gene duplication/fusions and the repeated motif is an RNA binding domain.

the modern protein synthesis factors have arisen through a process of gene duplication and fusion, which is consistent with the notion that the genetic material of the last common ancestor of the three super-kingdoms was more compact than the modern genome.
the modern protein synthesis factors are a result of gene fusion events and that the root of the protein superfamily tree is an ancestor of the IF-1 gene.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a single ancestral protein, IF-1, has evolved into a superfamily of related protein synthesis factors through a series of gene duplication/fusions events.
the protein synthesis apparatus is an ancient molecular machine that has been conserved throughout the evolution of life.
gene duplication/fusion can explain the evolutionary origin of protein synthesis factors and is an alternative to the more popular gene shuffling model.
